Full details: Description check

**Explanation** The description is complete and relevant. It includes the overview, DCO sign-off, validation results, test updates, reviewer starting point, and related issue. The unchecked documentation item includes an explanation that documentation changes are not applicable.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** [`#503`] Requirement: extract_json() must return valid JSON objects embedded in prose when string values contain unmatched { or } characters. Malformed JSON and top-level prose-wrapped arrays are not requirements. Head src/deep_researcher_agent/common/json_utils.py finds the first '{' and calls json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(text[start:]). The decoder, not a brace counter, sets the object end, so braces inside strings no longer affect the boundary. Invalid JSON from that point logs the existing warning and returns None. Head tests/deep_researcher_agent/common/test_json_utils.py adds a parametrized test with closing-brace, opening-brace, escaped-quote, nested-object, and nested-array string values wrapped in prose. It also adds a first-object-selection test. These cover the issue's example and listed failure classes. Existing TestExtractJson tests remain in the file. The PR-reported local run (22 passed, 5 new cases failing on develop) is author evidence only; I did not execute tests. The base blob for json_utils.py was unavailable, so the removed brace-counter lines were verified only through the issue and PR text, not a diff. Residual limitation, not a `#503` requirement: a non-JSON '{' before the intended object still causes failure, as the PR states.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** The whole-PR changes are limited to the extract_json() prose fallback and its docstring step 3 in json_utils.py, plus new and parametrized tests in test_json_utils.py. The docstring update and tests support the `#503` fix. The PR description's DCO and checklist text is not a code change. No unrelated source, configuration, or dependency changes appear in the reviewed evidence. The whole-PR diff could not be read because changed blobs were unavailable, so this verdict rests on the head file contents and head test file contents, and the stated scope of the PR.
Full details: Docstring Coverage

**Explanation** Docstring coverage is 100.00% which is sufficient. The required threshold is 80.00%. Docstring coverage is scoped to functions touched by this diff with cyclomatic complexity of at least 2. Documentation-only edits and deletions within surviving functions are included; unchanged diff context and fully deleted functions are excluded. Analyzed 1 functions across 2 files.
